failures.title: Ford R9DA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - 2012-Present
items.whatHappens: As a direct-injection engine, fuel does not wash over the intake valves, allowing oil vapour from the PCV system to bake onto the valves. This restricts airflow, causing rough idling, hesitation, and a noticeable loss of the ST's signature power.
items.repairVsReplace: A walnut blasting service can resolve this without engine removal. However, if ignored for extreme mileages, it can contribute to pre-ignition and piston damage, necessitating a full R9DA engine replacement.

items.title: Coolant System Leaks (Water Pump & Thermostat Housing) - 2012-Present
items.whatHappens: The plastic composite thermostat housing and water pump seals are known weak points on the 2.0 EcoBoost family. Cracks or seal degradation lead to external coolant leaks or internal mixing, risking rapid overheating and head gasket failure if warning lights are ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Early detection allows for a straightforward component replacement. If overheating has already warped the cylinder head, a reconditioned R9DA engine is the most reliable long-term solution.

items.title: Piston Ring Land Failure - Primarily on tuned or poorly maintained units
items.onset: 40,000-80,000 miles (accelerated by aggressive tuning or incorrect spark plugs)
items.whatHappens: The #4 piston is most susceptible to ring land cracking under high boost pressure or pre-ignition (knock). This results in severe misfires, blue smoke from the exhaust, and a catastrophic drop in cylinder compression.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a catastrophic failure. A simple repair is not viable; the engine must be replaced with a reconditioned or rebuilt R9DA unit featuring updated forged internals if the car remains tuned.

failures.goodYearsLine: The R9DA is generally robust when kept to factory specifications and serviced with the correct Ford WSS-M2C948-B 5W-30 oil. Facelift models and later production runs benefit from minor ECU and cooling system refinements, making severe bottom-end failures rare on unmodified cars.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement R9DA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used R9DA engine is a viable, budget-friendly option only if it comes with a verifiable service history proving timely oil changes and no history of aggressive tuning. Given the risk of hidden carbon buildup or early coolant leaks, ensure the seller can provide recent compression test results before purchase. Browse our vetted used engine suppliers.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most Focus ST and Mondeo owners, a reconditioned R9DA is the optimal balance of cost and reliability. A proper recon process will replace all coolant system plastics, install an updated water pump, clean or replace the high-pressure fuel pump, and fit a new timing chain assembly, directly addressing the R9DA engine problems outlined above. View reconditioned R9DA options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is strongly recommended if your original R9DA suffered piston ring land failure or if you intend to apply a performance tune (Stage 2 or higher). A quality rebuild will upgrade the pistons and connecting rods to forged components, ensuring the 2.0 EcoBoost can safely handle increased boost pressures without catastrophic failure. Explore custom rebuilt engine builds.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All quotes can be arranged as supply-only or full supply & fit through our network of UK specialists, complete with a minimum 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery. Learn more about our supply & fit service.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Ford Focus ST (Mk3) and Mondeo hold reasonable residual values, typically ranging from £4,000 to £12,000 depending on age and condition. A reconditioned R9DA engine replacement comfortably sits within this value band, making it a financially sound investment. However, for high-mileage examples with additional bodywork or transmission issues, evaluate the vehicle's overall scrap or part-ex value before committing to a major engine replacement.

items.question: How much does a Ford R9DA engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford R9DA engine typically costs between £1,800 and £3,200 for supply-only, with fully fitted replacements ranging from £2,450 to £3,850. Prices vary based on whether the turbocharger and high-pressure fuel pump are included or upgraded. Independent specialist labour usually adds 10-14 hours at £65-£85 per hour.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the R9DA engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are carbon buildup on the intake valves and coolant system leaks from the plastic thermostat housing or water pump. Direct injection means fuel does not clean the intake valves, leading to restricted airflow and misfires over time. Coolant leaks can cause rapid overheating and secondary head gasket damage if warning signs are ignored.

items.question: Which Ford models use the R9DA engine?
items.answer: The R9DA is a 2.0-litre turbocharged EcoBoost petrol engine primarily fitted to the Ford Focus ST (Mk3, 2012-2018) and select Ford Mondeo models (2013-2017). It produces 250 hp in the Focus ST application. Always verify your specific chassis fitment using your registration number before ordering parts.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned R9DA engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned R9DA is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the engine's known vulnerability to carbon buildup and cooling system degradation. Used engines carry the risk of hidden, pre-existing wear from aggressive tuning or missed oil services. A proper reconditioning process replaces all plastic coolant components, updates the water pump, and verifies turbocharger health.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the R9DA engine?
items.answer: The R9DA engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, visible near the transmission junction, and is listed on your V5C registration document. It is frequently confused with the later R9DC facelift variant, which requires different ECU mapping. Fitting the wrong revision can result in incorrect boost pressures and persistent check-engine lights.
